To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

ultra-high center-of mass collision energy can be attained in a charged particle collision in a stationary black hole background with degenerate horizons or non-degenerate horizons with multiple scattering mechanism, and the critical angular momentum or the critical charge are essential to get ultra high energy.

the ultra-high center of mass energy can be attained in a general stationary black hole with two-fold degenerated horizons if one particle is with critical angular momentum (or critical charge) and the remaining parameters of particles and the black hole satisfy some restrictions.

ultra-high center of mass energy can be reached by charged particle collision in the vicinity of a general stationary charged horizon, and the critical angular momentum or charged is essential to the existence of the ultra-high center of-mass energy without the fine-tuning problem.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a general class of stationary black holes, including the Kerr-Newman black hole and the small braneworld black holes.
the possibility of getting high center-of-masses energy in a general stationary black hole and the mechanism of ultra-high center-of mass energy.
the possibility of attaining infinite center-of-mass energies for colliding particles in general stationary charged black holes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

ultra-high energy is always available in a general stationary black hole, provided that the particle is with critical angular momentum and/or charge, and the black hole parameters satisfy certain restriction.
, the charged particle accelerator is possible to be built on any-fold degeneracy horizon of general stationary charged black holes.

, in general stationary charged black holes, the center-of-mass collision of two charged particles can be used as an effective charged particle accelerator to produce ultra-high energy, and the ultra-high energy can be attained without the fine-tuning of the parameters of black holes and the colliding particles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the ultra-high center of mass energy can be obtained by the charged particle collision in a charged black hole, provided the black hole has multiple-fold degenerate horizons or non-degenerate horizons.
the ultra-high energy collision of charged particles in a stationary charged black hole may be a good candidate to study the physics beyond the standard model.

ultra-high center-of mass energy can be obtained in a general charged black hole by choosing the appropriate particle parameters and the black hole parameters, provided that the black hole has degenerate horizons or the multiple scattering mechanism.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the ultra-high center of mass energy can be attained in the center-of-mass frame of colliding particles, provided that the particles have critical angular momentum or/and critical charge, and that the particles are close to the innermost stable circular orbits.

the ultra-high center of mass energy can be obtained in a generic charged black hole, provided that the black hole is sufficiently small and the particles have appropriate charges and angular momenta.

the ultra-high center of mass energy can be attained by colliding charged particles with critical angular momentum and/or critical charge in the center of a black hole, which is independent of the details of the black hole.
